submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the second or later token of a word or fixed name that the tokenizer has split, at the piece that completes a specific lexical unit begun by the preceding token(s): mostly technical, chemical and medical terms (opi|ates, ole|fin, hyp|ox|ia, gly|ox|al, poly|ure|thane, neutr|inos, self-im|posed), plus a few lexicalised multiword names (White House, Toy Story, free software, three-phase). It stays low (about 0.2-0.4 of max) on whole single-token words, on the first piece of a word, and on freely composed phrases such as 'White Horse' or 'new software'.

rival_explanations: Broader: it fires on any non-initial subword piece of any multi-token word, whatever the domain or how predictable the piece is. This predicts high activity on everyday split words and rare names (xylophone, Eiffel, transferable), where the hypothesis predicts low to moderate activity.

Predictability: it fires on any token that the preceding context makes near-certain, including whole-word bigrams. This predicts high activity on 'United States', 'New York' or 'prime minister', where the hypothesis predicts background level.
